question.text: Indus Special Situations Fund (Cat II) is valuing a distressed investee on break-up basis. Tangible net worth = INR 50 crore. Appreciation in inventory and intangibles on liquidation = INR 8 crore; Reduction in payables market value = INR 2 crore; Depreciation in fixed assets (scrap value) = INR 25 crore; Receivables haircut = INR 5 crore. Break-up value of business is:

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per PDF Illustration 11.4 Part II: Break-up Value = Tangible net worth + Additions (inventory/intangibles + payable reduction) - Deductions (FA scrap dep + receivables haircut) = 50 + (8 + 2) - (25 + 5) = 50 + 10 - 30 = INR 30 crore. **The Trap:** INR 40 ignores the receivables haircut; INR 28 double counts something; INR 35 forgets to add the payable reduction benefit. Break-up is LIQUIDATION basis: scrap value of FA, haircut on receivables, but MARKET reduction on payables is a benefit (you settle for less). **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests the same break-up framework. XV (RA) covers it under distressed equity research. Break-up value is the FLOOR; going-concern DCF is the CEILING in most Cat II distressed deals. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** In Cat II debt-to-special-situations deals, compute break-up value as your downside scenario for the IC. If your bid price = break-up value, the trade is essentially riskless on liquidation-day basis (assuming your security interest is perfected).
